author: claude
hypothesis: Profitable, conservatively accounted companies that are cheap relative to earnings and book value outperform the S&P 500 median over the next three months
rationale: Quality (gross profitability, low accruals) and value are among the few factor themes that replicate out of sample (Jensen, Kelly & Pedersen 2023) and, with quarterly turnover, survive trading costs (Novy-Marx & Velikov). Investors overpay for exciting growth and underweight dull, profitable firms; combining four related measures reduces the noise of any single accounting ratio
notes: Single factors in this composite were looked at individually on 2025-2026 in backfilled trials (all |t| < 1.2); the composite itself is new

author: claude
hypothesis: Stocks whose closest technology peers (by 10-K business description) rose more than they did over the past month outperform over the next month
rationale: Attention-constrained investors are slow to carry news across related firms: technology-linked returns predict focal returns (Lee, Sun, Wang & Zhang 2019, JFE; 117 bps/month alpha) and customer shocks predict supplier returns (Cohen & Frazzini 2008, JF). A theme lifting its leaders (e.g. AI data-centre demand) should reach the lagging firms in the same technology space with a delay
notes: Peers from a text encoder pinned to 2024-11-05 (all-mpnet-base-v2); evaluated with development through 2023 and holdout 2024-2026 at the user's request

author: claude
hypothesis: Companies whose customers (named in their own 10-K) had high returns last month outperform next month
rationale: Cohen & Frazzini (2008, JF): attention-constrained investors do not immediately price news about a firm's customers into the supplier, so customer returns predict supplier returns. Example of the mechanism: a big customer committing more volume to a supplier is good news the supplier's price absorbs slowly
notes: Links extracted by name matching in 10-K sentences with customer words; only S&P 500 customers are visible, so coverage is partial. Dev through 2023, holdout 2024-2026 at the user's request

author: claude
hypothesis: Earnings press releases whose wording resembles past releases that the market rewarded keep outperforming for weeks after the release
rationale: Post-earnings drift: investors underreact to earnings news (Bernard & Thomas 1989). Text adds what headline EPS misses (guidance, tone, one-offs); BlackRock trains models on call text labelled by market reaction for the same reason

rationale: Post-earnings drift: investors underreact to earnings news (Bernard & Thomas 1989). Text adds what headline EPS misses (guidance, tone, one-offs); BlackRock trains models on call text labelled by market reaction for the same reason

author: claude
hypothesis: Stocks with the highest 12-month returns, skipping the latest month, outperform over the next month, more so among mid and small caps
rationale: Investors underreact to gradual information and herd late (Jegadeesh & Titman 1993); the effect is weaker where analyst coverage is dense, so it should be stronger outside the S&P 500. Monthly rebalancing of a slow signal keeps turnover moderate
notes: Universe built from today's index members (survivorship bias); the S&P 500-only version of this factor was tested earlier (backfilled trials)

author: claude
hypothesis: Last month's biggest losers outperform last month's biggest winners over the next month, mostly among mid and small caps, but possibly not after trading costs
rationale: Short-term reversal compensates liquidity providers who absorb temporary order imbalances (Jegadeesh 1990; Nagel 2012). That makes it strongest exactly where trading is expensive, so the after-cost gate is the real test
notes: Universe built from today's index members (survivorship bias); the S&P 500-only version of this factor was tested earlier (backfilled trials)
